title: AI & Machine Learning Engineering
description: From linear algebra and classical ML through deep learning, transformers and LLM systems, ending with models you can actually deploy and monitor in production.

steps.title: Python for numerical work
steps.description: Get fluent with NumPy arrays, broadcasting, vectorised operations and pandas DataFrames. Nearly every ML library speaks these two, and loops you should have vectorised are the most common beginner bottleneck.

steps.title: Linear algebra you will actually use
steps.description: Vectors, matrix multiplication, rank, eigenvalues and the geometric meaning of a dot product. This is the language every model is written in — without it, backpropagation stays a black box.

steps.title: Calculus and gradients
steps.description: Derivatives, partial derivatives, the chain rule and gradient descent. You need enough to understand why a gradient points uphill and what a learning rate is really scaling.

steps.title: Probability and statistics
steps.description: Distributions, expectation, variance, Bayes' theorem, sampling and confidence intervals. Model evaluation is applied statistics, and most bad ML results are statistics mistakes.

steps.title: Exploratory data analysis
steps.description: Load a messy dataset and interrogate it: distributions, correlations, outliers, missing values. Plot before you model — most insight arrives in this step, not the training one.

steps.title: Data cleaning and feature engineering
steps.description: Handle missing data, encode categoricals, scale numerics, and build features that carry signal. Feature quality beats model choice more often than not.

steps.title: Supervised learning: regression
steps.description: Linear and polynomial regression, regularisation with Ridge and Lasso, and the bias-variance tradeoff. Understand why more capacity is not automatically better.

steps.title: Supervised learning: classification
steps.description: Logistic regression, k-NN, naive Bayes and support vector machines. Learn what each assumes about your data, because the assumption is what breaks first.

steps.title: Trees, forests and gradient boosting
steps.description: Decision trees, random forests, then XGBoost and LightGBM. Boosted trees still win most problems on tabular data — know them before reaching for a neural network.

steps.title: Model evaluation done properly
steps.description: Train/validation/test splits, cross-validation, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC and calibration. Learn what accuracy hides on imbalanced data.

steps.title: Overfitting, leakage and validation traps
steps.description: Data leakage, temporal leakage and fitting the test set through repeated tuning. This step is what separates a real result from a number that collapses in production.

steps.title: Unsupervised learning
steps.description: k-means, hierarchical clustering, DBSCAN, PCA and t-SNE. Useful when labels are scarce and essential for exploration and compression.

steps.title: Neural network fundamentals
steps.description: Perceptrons, activation functions, loss functions, forward and backward passes. Implement backpropagation once by hand — it pays for itself forever.

steps.title: PyTorch fundamentals
steps.description: Tensors, autograd, nn.Module, optimisers and the training loop. Write the loop yourself before adopting any framework that hides it.

steps.title: Training deep networks in practice
steps.description: Weight initialisation, batch normalisation, dropout, learning-rate schedules and early stopping. The theory is short; the practice is where models are won or lost.

steps.title: Convolutional neural networks
steps.description: Convolutions, pooling, receptive fields and classic architectures from LeNet to ResNet. Still the backbone of most vision work.

steps.title: Computer vision tasks
steps.description: Image classification, object detection and segmentation, plus augmentation strategies and transfer learning from pretrained backbones.

steps.title: Sequence models: RNNs and LSTMs
steps.description: Recurrent networks, vanishing gradients, LSTMs and GRUs. Largely superseded by transformers, but they explain why attention was invented.

steps.title: Attention and the transformer
steps.description: Self-attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding and the encoder-decoder stack. This is the single most important architecture to understand deeply today.

steps.title: NLP with pretrained models
steps.description: Tokenisation, embeddings, and fine-tuning BERT-family models for classification, NER and question answering using the Transformers library.

steps.title: Large language models
steps.description: Pretraining versus fine-tuning, instruction tuning, RLHF, context windows and sampling parameters. Understand what a model can and cannot know.

steps.title: Prompt engineering and structured output
steps.description: Few-shot prompting, chain-of-thought, system prompts and forcing schema-valid output. The cheapest lever on LLM quality before any fine-tuning.

steps.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
steps.description: Chunking, embeddings, vector stores and reranking. Build a RAG pipeline end to end and measure how retrieval quality dominates answer quality.

steps.title: Fine-tuning and parameter-efficient methods
steps.description: Full fine-tuning versus LoRA and QLoRA, dataset construction and evaluation. Know when fine-tuning genuinely beats prompting plus retrieval.

steps.title: Experiment tracking and reproducibility
steps.description: Version datasets, code, hyperparameters and metrics so a result can be reproduced months later. Seed everything and log everything.

steps.title: Model serving
steps.description: Wrap a model behind an API with FastAPI, handle batching, and understand latency, throughput and cold starts. A model nobody can call has no value.

steps.title: Containerising and deploying models
steps.description: Package the runtime with Docker, manage dependencies and GPU drivers, and deploy to a cloud target with sane resource limits.

steps.title: MLOps pipelines
steps.description: Automate data validation, training, evaluation and deployment so retraining is a pipeline run rather than an afternoon of notebooks.

steps.title: Monitoring and drift detection
steps.description: Track prediction distributions, data drift, concept drift and business metrics. Models rot quietly — instrumentation is how you notice.

steps.title: Optimisation and inference cost
steps.description: Quantisation, distillation, pruning, batching and caching. Turning a working model into an affordable one is its own engineering discipline.

steps.title: Responsible AI
steps.description: Bias measurement, fairness metrics, explainability with SHAP, privacy, and knowing where a model must not be used at all.

steps.title: Capstone: an end-to-end ML system
steps.description: Ship one system that owns its whole lifecycle: ingestion, training, evaluation, serving, monitoring and a retraining trigger. This is the portfolio piece that gets interviews.

title: Data Engineering
description: Build the pipelines and warehouses everything else depends on — SQL depth, batch and streaming ingestion, dimensional modelling, orchestration and data quality at scale.

steps.title: SQL fundamentals
steps.description: SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, subqueries and set operations until they are automatic. SQL is the one skill every data engineering role tests without exception.

steps.title: Advanced SQL
steps.description: Window functions, CTEs, recursive queries, pivots and correlated subqueries. Window functions in particular separate analysts from engineers.

steps.title: Query performance and indexing
steps.description: Read an EXPLAIN plan, understand B-tree versus hash indexes, and know why a query went from milliseconds to minutes after a schema change.

steps.title: Relational modelling and normalisation
steps.description: Keys, relationships, normal forms and when denormalisation is the right call. Schema mistakes compound for years.

steps.title: Python for data engineering
steps.description: File and API ingestion, generators for large files, type hints, testing and packaging. Pipelines are software and deserve software practices.

steps.title: Linux, shell and cron
steps.description: Navigate a filesystem, pipe between tools, read logs and schedule work. Data infrastructure lives on Linux and fails on Linux.

steps.title: Version control and code review
steps.description: Branching, pull requests and CI for data code. Pipelines edited directly in production are the root cause of most data incidents.

steps.title: Data formats and serialisation
steps.description: CSV, JSON, Avro, Parquet and ORC — row versus columnar layout, compression and schema evolution. Choosing Parquet over CSV can cut cost by an order of magnitude.

steps.title: Batch ingestion
steps.description: Pull from APIs, databases and files with idempotent, restartable jobs. Design for the day the source is down halfway through a run.

steps.title: Change data capture
steps.description: Replicate database changes with log-based CDC instead of full reloads, and understand the ordering and delete semantics it brings.

steps.title: Data warehouses
steps.description: Columnar warehouses, partitioning, clustering and cost models in BigQuery, Snowflake or Redshift. Learn how a warehouse actually bills you.

steps.title: Dimensional modelling
steps.description: Facts, dimensions, star schemas and slowly changing dimensions. Kimball's model remains the default vocabulary of analytics.

steps.title: ELT and transformation with dbt
steps.description: Model transformations as version-controlled SQL with tests, documentation and lineage. dbt is the industry default for the T in ELT.

steps.title: Data quality and testing
steps.description: Assert freshness, uniqueness, referential integrity and distribution expectations, and fail the pipeline loudly when they break.

steps.title: Workflow orchestration
steps.description: Model pipelines as DAGs with dependencies, retries, backfills and SLAs in Airflow or an equivalent. Orchestration is where reliability is won.

steps.title: Idempotency and backfills
steps.description: Design jobs that can be rerun safely for any date range. Partition by time and make writes atomic — you will backfill more than you expect.

steps.title: Distributed processing with Spark
steps.description: RDDs, DataFrames, lazy evaluation, shuffles and partitioning. Understand why a shuffle is expensive and how skew ruins a job.

steps.title: Spark tuning
steps.description: Partition sizing, broadcast joins, caching and the Spark UI. Reading the UI is the fastest route from a slow job to a fast one.

steps.title: Streaming with Kafka
steps.description: Topics, partitions, consumer groups, offsets and delivery guarantees. The foundation of every real-time data platform.

steps.title: Stream processing semantics
steps.description: Event time versus processing time, windowing, watermarks and exactly-once processing. Streaming correctness is subtle and worth the study.

steps.title: Data lakes and lakehouse tables
steps.description: Object storage layouts plus ACID table formats such as Delta Lake, Iceberg and Hudi that bring transactions and time travel to files.

steps.title: Infrastructure as code
steps.description: Provision warehouses, buckets and clusters declaratively with Terraform so environments are reproducible and reviewable.

steps.title: Containers and deployment
steps.description: Package pipeline code in Docker images and run them on a scheduler or Kubernetes with pinned dependencies.

steps.title: Data governance and cataloguing
steps.description: Ownership, lineage, discoverability and documentation. A dataset nobody can find or trust may as well not exist.

steps.title: Security, privacy and compliance
steps.description: Encryption, least-privilege access, PII handling, masking and retention policies under GDPR-style regimes.

steps.title: Cost engineering
steps.description: Partition pruning, storage tiering, query cost attribution and killing runaway jobs. Data platforms fail budget reviews before they fail technically.

steps.title: Observability for pipelines
steps.description: Metrics, logging, alerting and freshness dashboards, so you learn about a broken pipeline before your stakeholders do.

steps.title: Serving data to consumers
steps.description: Semantic layers, BI tool integration, reverse ETL and APIs over curated tables. The last mile is where value is realised.

steps.title: Capstone: a production data platform
steps.description: Ingest from a live API into a lakehouse, transform with dbt, orchestrate with Airflow, test with expectations and expose a dashboard — all in code, all reproducible.
